openDecisions.title: Organization deployments
openDecisions.text: jive provision installs a resource component into the organization's own Convex deployment (app.use in its generated convex.config.ts, then a deploy). Open: how each organization's deployment is created and who holds its deploy key.

openDecisions.title: DNS API shape
options: Declarative: setRecords declares every record one owner (a resource instance) wants in a zone; the connector creates, updates and removes to match, touching only that owner's records, which the component tracks in its own table (recommended).
Imperative: ensureRecord adds one record; removing one is a separate call or left to a person.

packages.name: @jive-sh/server
packages.purpose: Database + credential holder (Convex). Deployed. Extends jive-abstract-backend-convex. People sign in with their jive.sh passkey; every call takes a session token, which a CLI or daemon gets by claiming a sign-in request approved on jive.sh/login. Holds each account's SSH key (ed25519, sealed like connections; built 2026-11-01): ssh:sign takes a session token and the bytes an SSH agent was asked to sign, for git commits and SSH logins alike, and returns the signature. Decided 2026-11-01, Alex: "There's just an ssh sign request. You don't create keys. You can fetch the public key or sign", and "when someone signs up, they can create public keys but they don't make new ssh keys. Jive will manage key rotation". So the public SSH API is ssh:publicKey and ssh:sign, with no ssh:createKey; Jive makes each account's key pair at sign-up and rotates it. Decided 2026-11-01, Alex: "I think a session should only be obtainable via human passkey, cicd oidc token exchange, or jive mints a token and hands it off to a compute provider running an agent workflow. So three methods and only 2 of them are available via cli". Today: passkey is built (in the browser, and for programs through sign-in requests); the CI/CD OIDC exchange is built (0.5.0, 2026-11-01: pipelineSessions:signIn turns a deploy job's GitHub ID token into a one-hour session for its registered code repository, and packages:provision takes that session token; jive-abstract-library 0.8.0 calls both); minting for a compute provider is not built and depends on the compute resource kind. A test fails if any other code opens a session. Decided 2026-11-06, Alex: "Let's do session length of a day and then the each use you talked about extends the expiry to a day after that moment of use". So a person's session ends a day after sign-in, and every mutation or action that acts with it (each ssh:sign above all) moves its end to a day after that call; queries cannot write in Convex, so ssh:publicKey and accounts:me check without extending, and accounts:me returns the current end as sessionExpiresAt. No upper limit: a session used at least daily never ends until signed out. Pipeline sessions keep their fixed hour. Built in @jive-sh/server 0.12.0 (2026-11-06). Decided 2026-11-01, Alex (his idea: "both the ssh thing and the passkey thing could go into a convex component"): one Convex component installed in @jive-sh/server holds each account's private keys sealed in its own tables (ed25519 for SSH signing, P-256 for passkeys) and signs from a Node action given a session token; the server's SSH keys move into it, and @jive-sh/cloud-sk is retired once it lands. Being built by Grok's thread

packages.name: @jive-sh/jive
packages.purpose: The jive CLI + the shared CI/CD pipeline. Replaces @ozyman42/ozy-cli (0.3.0, 2026-11-01): jive login (passkey sign-in request, which also fetches the account's public key) and jive login --cicd (GitHub OIDC for a pipeline session) are the only ways to a session; jive init and jive load configure each repository to sign and push through the agent (jive never signs in to GitHub); jive git setup was removed in 0.3.0 (Alex, 2026-11-01: "git setup probably goes away honestly"), and the code-repository connector is to derive each package's git URL; jive-signing-agent holds no key and forwards each sign request to @jive-sh/server ssh:sign; Decided 2026-11-06, Alex, on whether jive login should write the account key and a github.com block into ~/.ssh: "Well I think maybe this current design is better. I think the reason I was having ozy-cli write to ~/.ssh was so it could be used for other ssh things, not just cloneing but commit signing and ssh sign-in unrelated to github. But the ssh config change really only ever set it up for github. Perhaps people could get used to reaching into ~/.jive/account.pub to use their jive key for other things". So jive never writes to ~/.ssh: signing and GitHub SSH stay configured per repository by jive init and jive load (user.signingKey, and core.sshCommand with IdentityAgent and IdentityFile), and a person uses the key for anything else by pointing ssh or ssh-keygen at ~/.jive/ssh/account.pub (the path he meant) and ~/.jive/signing-agent.sock, as the README shows; jive ssh connect and jive ssh sign (Alex, 2026-11-06: "Can there be a jive ssh command which runs ssh using the correct pubkey, identities only, signing agent settings?") run ssh and ssh-keygen -Y sign with those options, built by the same code as core.sshCommand, passing every word after connect or sign through (jive-abstract-library 0.14.0 Cli.passThroughCommand); jive link was removed in 0.7.0 (Alex: "init sets up linking too"); jive-extension-daemon (built 2026-11-05; Alex: "That was supposed to be a daemon inside the @jive-sh/jive package") answers the Jive browser extension through Chrome native messaging and the jive-native-host command, with the one session jive login keeps (it signs in through the same sign-in request, and SignOut forgets that session), replacing a separate daemon package, which was never published and is deleted; jive daemons, jive upgrade. Next: jive provision <kind> <instance> (e.g. connector-package-registry @jive-sh/server-client), the organization picking the implementation, which the deploy hook will run after jive login --cicd

packages.name: jive-abstract-resource
packages.purpose: Defines a kind of resource an organization owns, as a Convex component. Decided 2026-11-01: each resource kind is a connector abstract with a standard "make sure this exists" call; an implementation is a library shipping the component; instances are declared in the package's jive block and held as records in that component; jive provision lists resource packages by the jive-resource- prefix. Decided 2026-11-01, Alex: "We have a deploy hook in CI. That should do a `jive login --cicd` then `jive provision` for a given resource", and "it should probably only be provisioning the abstract. so `jive provision connector-package-registry` and then it talks to the jive org which should have one impl configured". So a caller names the resource kind and the instance; each organization configures exactly one implementation per kind; this generic call replaces packages:provision on @jive-sh/server

packages.name: jive-abstract-resource-connector
packages.purpose: Resources that connect to one outside system. Decided 2026-11-01, Alex: "Connectors must expose an API which allows for key rotation". So every connector whose system holds a copy of a key (e.g. jive-resource-connector-code-repository-github, which holds the account's SSH key) exposes a standard rotation call, and a rotation reaches every system
